legend: Jury has hidden a permutation p of integers from 0 to n - 1. You know only the length n. Remind that in permutation all integers are distinct.

Let b be the inverse permutation for p, i.e. pbi = i for all i. The only thing you can do is to ask xor of elements pi and bj, printing two indices i and j (not necessarily distinct). As a result of the query with indices i and j you'll get the value ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png), where ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png) denotes the xor operation. You can find the description of xor operation in notes.

Note that some permutations can remain indistinguishable from the hidden one, even if you make all possible n2 queries. You have to compute the number of permutations indistinguishable from the hidden one, and print one of such permutations, making no more than 2n queries.
The hidden permutation does not depend on your queries.
input: The first line contains single integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 5000) — the length of the hidden permutation. You should read this integer first.
output: When your program is ready to print the answer, print three lines.
In the first line print "!".
In the second line print single integer answers_cnt — the number of permutations indistinguishable from the hidden one, including the hidden one.
In the third line print n integers p0, p1, ..., pn - 1 (0 ≤ pi < n, all pi should be distinct) — one of the permutations indistinguishable from the hidden one.
Your program should terminate after printing the answer.

To ask about xor of two elements, print a string "? i j", where i and j — are integers from 0 to n - 1 — the index of the permutation element and the index of the inverse permutation element you want to know the xor-sum for. After that print a line break and make flush operation.
After printing the query your program should read single integer — the value of ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png).

For a permutation of length n your program should make no more than 2n queries about xor-sum. Note that printing answer doesn't count as a query. Note that you can't ask more than 2n questions. If you ask more than 2n questions or at least one incorrect question, your solution will get "Wrong answer".

If at some moment your program reads -1 as an answer, it should immediately exit (for example, by calling exit(0)). You will get "Wrong answer" in this case, it means that you asked more than 2n questions, or asked an invalid question. If you ignore this, you can get other verdicts since your program will continue to read from a closed stream.
Your solution will get "Idleness Limit Exceeded", if you don't print anything or forget to flush the output, including for the final answer .
To flush you can use (just after printing line break):
fflush(stdout) in C++;
System.out.flush() in Java;
stdout.flush() in Python;
flush(output) in Pascal;
For other languages see the documentation.
Hacking
For hacking use the following format:
n
Contestant programs will not be able to see this input.
note: xor operation, or bitwise exclusive OR, is an operation performed over two integers, in which the i-th digit in binary representation of the result is equal to 1 if and only if exactly one of the two integers has the i-th digit in binary representation equal to 1. For more information, see here.

In the first example p = [0, 1, 2], thus b = [0, 1, 2], the values ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png) are correct for the given i, j. There are no other permutations that give the same answers for the given queries.
The answers for the queries are:

In the second example p = [3, 1, 2, 0], and b = [3, 1, 2, 0], the values ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png) match for all pairs i, j. But there is one more suitable permutation p = [0, 2, 1, 3], b = [0, 2, 1, 3] that matches all n2 possible queries as well. All other permutations do not match even the shown queries.

output.ai: 当你的程序准备好输出答案时，请输出三行。
第一行输出“!”。
第二行输出一个整数 answers_cnt——与隐藏排列无法区分的排列数量，其中包括隐藏排列本身。
在第三行输出 n 个整数 p0，p1，...，pn - 1（0 ≤ pi < n，所有 pi 应当互不相同）——一个与隐藏排列无法区分的排列。
输出答案后，程序应当终止。
若要询问两个元素的异或和，请输出字符串“? i j”，其中 i 和 j 是 0 到 n - 1 之间的整数，分别表示你想查询的排列元素下标和逆排列元素下标。之后输出换行并执行刷新操作。
输出询问后，程序应当读入一个整数——![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png) 的值。
对于一个长度为 n 的排列，程序询问异或和的次数不得超过 2n。注意，输出答案不计入询问次数。注意，你不能询问超过 2n 次。如果询问次数超过 2n，或至少有一个询问不正确，你的解法将获得“Wrong answer”。
如果程序在某个时刻读入的答案为 -1，应立即退出（例如调用 exit(0)）。在这种情况下，你将获得“Wrong answer”，这意味着你询问了超过 2n 次，或提出了无效询问。如果忽略这一点，由于程序会继续从已关闭的输入流中读取数据，你可能会得到其他评测结果。
如果你不输出任何内容或忘记刷新输出（包括最终答案），你的程序将获得“空闲时间超限”（Idleness Limit Exceeded）。
你可以使用以下方式进行刷新（就在输出换行后）：
C++ 中的 `fflush(stdout)`；
Java 中的 `System.out.flush()`；
Python 中的 `stdout.flush()`；
Pascal 中的 `flush(output)`；
其他语言请参阅文档。
Hack
进行 Hack 时请使用以下格式：
n
参赛者程序将无法看到此输入。

legend.ai: 评测者隐藏了一个由 0 到 n - 1 的整数构成的排列 p。你只知道它的长度 n。提醒一下，排列中的所有整数都互不相同。

设 b 是 p 的逆排列，即对于所有 i，都有 pbi = i。你唯一能做的是询问元素 pi 和 bj 的异或值，并输出两个下标 i 和 j(不一定互不相同)。对于下标 i 和 j 的查询，你将得到数值 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png)，其中 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c4b7092c0f7ce6535f2574569c98f7b3c2fe2c5f.png) 表示异或运算。你可以在注释中找到异或运算的定义。
注意，即使你进行了所有可能的 n2 次询问，仍然可能有一些排列与隐藏排列无法区分。你需要计算与隐藏排列无法区分的排列数量，并输出其中一个这样的排列，且询问次数不超过 2n 次。
隐藏排列不依赖于你的询问。

input.ai: 第一行包含一个整数 n（1 ≤ n ≤ 5000）——隐藏排列的长度。你应当先读入这个整数。

note.ai: 异或运算，即按位异或，是对两个整数进行的一种运算：结果的二进制表示中的第 i 位为 1，当且仅当这两个整数的二进制表示中恰好有一个的第 i 位为 1。更多信息请参见此处。
在第一个样例中，p = [0, 1, 2]，因此 b = [0, 1, 2]，对于给定的 i 和 j，![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png) 这些值是正确的。不存在其他排列能为给定的查询给出相同的答案。

在第二个样例中，p = [3, 1, 2, 0]，且 b = [3, 1, 2, 0]，对于所有 i、j 对，数值 ![](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5dae53b8ed0e62c9af6c21130fc022b384e359ff.png) 都匹配。不过，还有一个合适的排列 p = [0, 2, 1, 3]，b = [0, 2, 1, 3]，它同样满足全部 n² 个可能的查询。其他所有排列甚至无法匹配题目中展示的查询。
